messages.author: cbe06beab2c3f853
messages.subject: Processing replicates vs. Injection replicates
parts:
Hi

I have an experiment including biological replicates, processing replicates (same biological samples, processed twice) and injections replicates (replicate MS runs of the same sample). Is it possible to differentiate between processing replicates and injection replicates?

Many thanks
Marc

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Processing replicates vs. Injection replicates
parts:
MSstats considers both as technical replicates. ( not distinguish two differently)

-Meena

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Processing replicates vs. Injection replicates
parts:
To elaborate a little:

You are correct, process replicates and injection replicates have different sources of variation.

The right way to do this would be to (1) summarize protein abundance into one number per protein per run, and (2) fit a linear mixed effects model that reflects your experiment: it has a term for biological replication, a term for process replication, and the error term for MS injection. This can be done in R, but unfortunately is not automated in MSstats

A second workaround this is to summarize protein abundance into one number per protein per *process replicate*, and then use regular MSstats. In practice, this would mean averaging log-abundances per protein per run across all the injections of a same process.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Olga

messages.author: 659ec85b628948d3
messages.subject: Re: Processing replicates vs. Injection replicates
parts:
Hi Olga and Marc,

interesting question.

For my SWATH experiments (50 biological replicate each injected 3 times - 150 injections) I've done a variation of Olga's second workaround suggestion.
Olga, would you agree with the approach below?

1) normalise ion data by Area under curve of each run
2) From my triplicate injection replicates (3x50 biological replicates) I chose the median of a given ion intensity to get back to my 50 biological replicates,
3) sum to peptides and proteins,
4) log2 transformed the protein data to do my stats on the protein level.

Olga, is there a published R script for your first suggestion to (1) summarize protein abundance into one number per protein per run, and (2) fit a linear mixed effects model that reflects your experiment?
Or would you be happy to share this?

Regards
Moe

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Processing replicates vs. Injection replicates
parts:
Hi Moe,

If you only have one layer of technical replication (injection replicates), you can use MSstats as is - there is no need to summarize. MSstats can deal with that.

The difference in the previous question was that in addition to the biological variation it has two layers of technical variation (sample prep replicates, and multiple injection replicates per sample prep). MSstats can automatically deal with one layer of technical replication, but not two. Therefore my suggestion was to summarize (e.g., using a median) the lowest level of technical replication (i.e., injection), and work with MSstats from that point on.

I definitely do not recommend summing peptides to proteins - MSstats is designed specifically to do a better job on that.

HTH
Olga
